summary.oneLiner: A clean, cash-led start: **presales ₹787cr (+20%)**, collections ₹409cr (+17%), reported **EBITDA ₹67cr (+40%, margin 35%, +9.5pp)** and **PAT ₹42cr (+26%, margin 22%)** — all achieved with **no launches in the quarter**, which is the most interesting fact on the call. Aspirational luxury (Naigaon, Kalyan) picked up on lower interest rates. Net cash surplus **₹193cr (+79%)** even after **₹170cr of business-development spend**, with net debt/equity at **0.07x** and an **AA** rating. Management reaffirmed **25–30% presales growth for FY27** and, notably, disclosed a **presentation error** on the GDV table when an analyst caught it. The one unresolved item is **Dubai** — launch-ready with all approvals, but deliberately held back.

financial scorecard (q1 fy27):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Presales | **₹787cr** | **+20%** (₹657cr) | **achieved with zero launches in the quarter** |
| Collections | **₹409cr** | **+17%** (₹351cr) | trailing-12-month collections ~**₹1,500cr** |
| Operating revenue | **₹191cr** | +2% (₹188cr) | revenue recognition lags presales by design |
| EBITDA / margin | **₹67cr · 35%** | **+40%**, margin **+9.5pp** | |
| PAT / margin | **₹42cr · 22%** | **+26%**, margin **+4.2pp** | |
| Net cash flow surplus | **₹193cr** | **+79%** | **after** deploying ₹170cr on BD and land capex |
| Net debt/equity | **0.07x** | negligible | **AA** long-term rating (India Ratings, Fitch Group) |
| Presales segment mix | Uber luxury **29%** · Premium luxury **50%** (₹391cr) · Aspirational luxury **21%** | balanced | |
| Embedded EBITDA margin on presales | **35–40%** on both FY26 and Q1FY27 presales | — | flows to reported profitability as projects reach revenue recognition |
| ESG | **GRESB 99/100** (green 5-star) vs benchmark 68; **S&P Global DJSI ESG 78/100** vs benchmark 30 | — | |
| GDV (new 3-way disclosure) | **Launched** / **To-be-launched (~₹16,100cr incl. ₹9,000cr Dubai)** / **Upcoming for launch** | first time split | ex-Dubai to-be-launched ≈ **₹7,100cr** |
> Notes: management explicitly runs the business "on cash flow, not accounting revenue" — reported operating revenue (+2%) materially understates the quarter, since presales grew 20% and the embedded 35–40% margin only reaches the P&L at revenue recognition. **The GDV table definition is wrong in the presentation** — "to-be launched" is labelled as projects under the approval process, but includes Dubai which has *all* approvals; the MD accepted the correction on the call and committed to edit it.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Presales growth: 25–30% for FY27** — reaffirmed twice despite Q1 at +20%: "we are confident overall in the full year, we will match our… guidance of 25% to 30% growth in our presales. Considering the full year of '27, we'll be at least 25% to 30% higher than the last year."
- **Collections: "similar growth, I would say, 25% to 30%"** for the year.
- **Launches this financial year: ~₹7,000–7,100cr of GDV (excluding Dubai)** — ODC additional tower; Andheri redevelopment (near Western Express Highway); **Sunteck Park Mira Road 2**; **one more tower at Vasai**; **1–2 towers at Naigaon**; **Sunteck Sky Park 2** and **Tower 2 at Sunteck City** specifically in the coming quarter.
- **Business development spend: to exceed FY26's >₹800cr** — "we are looking to, in fact, surpass this number… definitely this year also much more than the last year." ₹170cr already spent in Q1. Expect "some good acquisition BD announcements for sure."
- **Deliveries in FY27:** **Sunteck OneWorld**, plus new floors at **4th Avenue**, **1st Avenue** and **Pinnacle** — all to be constructed and delivered within the year, completing in **3–6 months** and monetised in the current year. Described as "substantial, very large delivery."
- **5th Avenue ODC:** residential construction started, **delivery ~3 years from now**; **commercial to start very soon and complete in 24–30 months** (presentation shows commercial revenue rising to ₹450cr by FY29).
- **Dubai (₹9,000cr GDV):** all regulatory approvals in place, project **launch-ready**; **timing recalibrated due to the ongoing situation** — no FY27/FY28 commitment given. Investment to date only **~₹200–225cr, no debt on the project**; surplus cash flow intended to be **repatriated to India for group growth**.
- **Fundraising:** the ₹2,000cr+ debt/equity board resolution is an **annual enabling resolution only** — "as on today, if you ask me, there is absolutely no planning of any fundraising."
- **Nepean Sea Road:** the big collections trigger once construction starts; RERA status not confirmed on the call.
order book & pipeline:
- **GDV now disclosed in three buckets** — Launched (approvals received, already launched); To-be-launched (**~₹16,100cr incl. ₹9,000cr Dubai → ~₹7,100cr domestic**); Upcoming for launch (planning and design stage). Management states the existing GDV gives "several years of launch visibility without considering any new acquisitions."
- **FY27 launch slate (~₹7,100cr domestic)**: ODC additional tower, Andheri redevelopment, Sunteck Park Mira Road 2, Vasai tower, Naigaon 1–2 towers — with Sunteck Sky Park 2 and Sunteck City Tower 2 in the very next quarter.
- **BD pipeline**: ₹170cr deployed in Q1 (Nepean Sea, Mira Road 2, certain redevelopment projects), some as token money; deals "already under negotiation or in the advanced stage."
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Aspirational luxury (21% of presales)** — the quarter's positive surprise, driven by **Naigaon and Kalyan**, attributed to **lower interest rates** and early signs of recovery. Management is "very bullish on now Kalyan picking up more strongly" and wants to monetise the large GDV there quickly. Notably, **both projects sold well with no launch in the quarter**.
- **Premium luxury (50%, ₹391cr)** — Sunteck City Goregaon, Sunteck Sky Park Mira Road, and Sunteck Beach Residences (SBR) all contributed. SBR was the only launch in the recent past.
- **Uber luxury (29%)** — includes the Nepean Sea Road asset, whose construction start is the identified step-change for collections.
- **Commercial (5th Avenue ODC)** — residential construction started; commercial to begin "very soon," 24–30 month build for a "spatial commercial"; presentation shows commercial revenue reaching ₹450cr by FY29.
- **Dubai SPV** — prime Downtown Dubai land next to Dubai Mall in the Burj Khalifa community; ~₹9,000cr GDV; **only ~₹200–225cr invested, zero project debt**; healthy land-cost-to-GDV; "highly profitable irrespective of the situation."
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Dubai as a low-cost, high-convexity option**: ~₹200–225cr of capital committed against ₹9,000cr of GDV, no debt, all approvals done, launch-ready — and the intent is to **repatriate the surplus to India for group growth**. The optionality costs almost nothing to hold.
- **Redevelopment** — Andheri (Western Express Highway) plus "certain redevelopment projects" funded within the Q1 ₹170cr BD spend.
- **Aggressive land banking / BD** — FY26 was the highest-ever BD year at >₹800cr, and FY27 is guided to surpass it, funded off a net-cash balance sheet.
- **Commercial rental annuity** at 5th Avenue ODC ramping to ₹450cr by FY29.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Balance sheet as the competitive weapon**: net debt/equity **0.07x**, **AA** rating from India Ratings (Fitch Group) — described as "among the strongest in Indian real estate" — while simultaneously generating a ₹193cr net cash surplus *after* ₹170cr of BD. This is what lets Sunteck buy land through a soft patch and hold Dubai off-market indefinitely.
- **Embedded margin already locked**: 35–40% EBITDA margin sits inside FY26 and Q1FY27 presales, so future reported profitability is substantially pre-determined by sales already made, not by future pricing.
- **ESG leadership as a genuine differentiator**: **GRESB 99/100** (benchmark 68) and **DJSI 78/100** (benchmark 30) — top-decile globally, and increasingly a screen for institutional capital and premium tenants.
- **Cash-flow-first operating discipline**, stated explicitly and consistently: "we run the business on cash flow, not accounting revenue."
margins & cost dynamics:
- **Reported EBITDA margin 35% (+9.5pp YoY)** and **PAT margin 22% (+4.2pp)** on nearly flat operating revenue — i.e. the margin expansion is mix and project-stage driven, not volume driven.
- **Embedded EBITDA margin of 35–40%** on both FY26 and Q1FY27 presales is the forward margin anchor; management ties reported profitability directly to revenue-recognition timing on those presales.
- The **balanced segment mix** (29/50/21) is presented as the reason the embedded margin holds — aspirational luxury growth has not diluted the blend.
- No input-cost or construction-cost commentary was offered on this call.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **₹170cr BD/land capex in Q1**; FY27 total guided to **exceed FY26's >₹800cr**.
- **Deliveries within FY27**: Sunteck OneWorld + additional floors at 4th Avenue, 1st Avenue and Pinnacle — each completing in **3–6 months** and to be monetised in-year.
- **5th Avenue ODC**: residential ~3 years to delivery; commercial 24–30 months from a start that is "very soon."
- **Dubai is the live slippage item** — launch-ready but deliberately deferred; when asked directly whether it lands in FY27 or FY28, management would not commit: "whenever the market is there, we will immediately launch."
- **Nepean Sea Road** construction start is the collections trigger; timing not given.
capital allocation:
- **Net cash surplus ₹193cr generated after ₹170cr of BD spend** — the clearest statement of the operating model: BD is funded out of operating cash, not leverage.
- **Net debt/equity 0.07x**; AA rated; **no fundraising planned** — the ₹2,000cr+ board resolution is a routine annual enabler taken every year.
- Dubai surplus, when it comes, is earmarked for **repatriation into India for group growth**.
- BD is countercyclical by intent — FY26 was a record year and FY27 is guided higher.
risks & watch-items:
1. **Dubai timing is entirely discretionary and open-ended.** ₹9,000cr of the ₹16,100cr "to-be-launched" GDV — over half — is a project management explicitly will not date. Any GDV-based valuation must haircut this.
2. **Q1 presales grew 20% against a 25–30% full-year guide** — the gap must be made up in the remaining three quarters, and it depends on the ₹7,100cr launch slate landing on schedule.
3. **Presentation error on the GDV definition**, self-acknowledged. Minor in substance, but it means the new three-way GDV disclosure needs re-reading once corrected.
4. **Collections lag presales structurally**, and the step-change depends on **Nepean Sea Road construction starting** — RERA status was asked about and not answered.
5. **Revenue-recognition optics**: operating revenue up only 2% YoY. Anyone reading the P&L rather than the cash flow will misjudge the quarter in both directions.
6. **Aspirational-luxury strength is rate-dependent** — management attributed it to lower interest rates; a rate reversal removes the driver.
7. **Rising BD spend against a soft launch cadence** — capital going into land while launches are pending is the classic real-estate timing risk, mitigated here by the net-cash position.
8. **Very short call (30 minutes)** with limited disclosure on construction costs, inventory, or project-level unsold stock.
management quality / tone: Confident and cash-focused, with a notable moment of integrity: when an analyst pointed out that the presentation's "to-be-launched GDV" definition (projects under approval) contradicted the statement that Dubai has all approvals, Kamal Khetan **immediately conceded** — "I appreciate your comment. You're totally right… I think we'll have to edit that" — rather than defending the slide. He also declined to date Dubai despite being pushed twice, which is the honest answer for a discretionary launch. The proactive move to split GDV into three buckets is a real disclosure improvement made unprompted. Against that, the call ran only 30 minutes with two questions per participant, and several follow-ups (new BD, Nepean Sea RERA) were cut off by the moderator on time.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Zero launches, +20% presales.** The quarter's growth came entirely from existing inventory — and specifically from Naigaon and Kalyan in the aspirational segment. That is a demand signal, not an inventory-release signal, and it makes the 25–30% full-year guide more credible once the ₹7,100cr slate actually launches.
- **Dubai is a ~₹200–225cr option on ₹9,000cr of GDV with no project debt.** The cost of waiting is negligible, which is exactly why management can afford to be patient. Treat it as an out-of-the-money option, not as pipeline.
- **The P&L is a lagging indicator by construction.** Presales +20%, embedded margin 35–40%, reported revenue +2% — the 35% reported EBITDA margin is the *past* flowing through, and today's presales set FY28–29 profitability.
- **BD spend rising into a launch year, funded from operating cash surplus**, is the tell on management's cycle view: they are buying while generating ₹193cr of surplus, not despite it.
- **ESG scores of 99/100 GRESB and 78/100 DJSI against benchmarks of 68 and 30** are far enough above peers to be a genuine institutional-capital differentiator, not boilerplate.
- The **₹2,000cr+ enabling resolution is routine** — management pre-empted the dilution question by noting it is taken every year with no fundraising planned.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.

hero.oneLiner: A clean, cash-led start: **presales ₹787cr (+20%)**, collections ₹409cr (+17%), reported **EBITDA ₹67cr (+40%, margin 35%, +9.5pp)** and **PAT ₹42cr (+26%, margin 22%)** — all achieved with **no launches in the quarter**, which is the most interesting fact on the call. Aspirational luxury (Naigaon, Kalyan) picked up on lower interest rates. Net cash surplus **₹193cr (+79%)** even after **₹170cr of business-development spend**, with net debt/equity at **0.07x** and an **AA** rating. Management reaffirmed **25–30% presales growth for FY27** and, notably, disclosed a **presentation error** on the GDV table when an analyst caught it. The one unresolved item is **Dubai** — launch-ready with all approvals, but deliberately held back.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Founder-led, Professionally-managed. Built by first-generation entrepreneur Mr. Kamal Khetan, who pioneered corporate business centres in BKC before creating Sunteck's real estate platform."
- "15+ years of delivery. 20 projects completed across multiple MMR cycles", with ~50+ msf acquired since inception and ~36 mn sq ft added since 2018.
- "Risk managed by design. Deliberately spread across micro-markets, development models (outright, JV / JDA, redevelopment) and customer segments - uber luxury to aspirational luxury."
- "Long visibility of growth. GDV of ~Rs 42,700 cr - several years of launches already secured, before any new acquisition."
- Ten micro-markets: BKC, Nepean Sea, Andheri, Goregaon (W), Borivali (W), Mira Road, Vasai (W), Naigaon, Kalyan and Downtown Dubai (international).

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Aspirational luxury (21% of presales)** — the quarter's positive surprise, driven by **Naigaon and Kalyan**, attributed to **lower interest rates** and early signs of recovery. Management is "very bullish on now Kalyan picking up more strongly" and wants to monetise the large GDV there quickly. Notably, **both projects sold well with no launch in the quarter**.
- **Premium luxury (50%, ₹391cr)** — Sunteck City Goregaon, Sunteck Sky Park Mira Road, and Sunteck Beach Residences (SBR) all contributed. SBR was the only launch in the recent past.
- **Uber luxury (29%)** — includes the Nepean Sea Road asset, whose construction start is the identified step-change for collections.
- **Commercial (5th Avenue ODC)** — residential construction started; commercial to begin "very soon," 24–30 month build for a "spatial commercial"; presentation shows commercial revenue reaching ₹450cr by FY29.
- **Dubai SPV** — prime Downtown Dubai land next to Dubai Mall in the Burj Khalifa community; ~₹9,000cr GDV; **only ~₹200–225cr invested, zero project debt**; healthy land-cost-to-GDV; "highly profitable irrespective of the situation."

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- **GDV now disclosed in three buckets** — Launched (approvals received, already launched); To-be-launched (**~₹16,100cr incl. ₹9,000cr Dubai → ~₹7,100cr domestic**); Upcoming for launch (planning and design stage). Management states the existing GDV gives "several years of launch visibility without considering any new acquisitions."
- **FY27 launch slate (~₹7,100cr domestic)**: ODC additional tower, Andheri redevelopment, Sunteck Park Mira Road 2, Vasai tower, Naigaon 1–2 towers — with Sunteck Sky Park 2 and Sunteck City Tower 2 in the very next quarter.
- **BD pipeline**: ₹170cr deployed in Q1 (Nepean Sea, Mira Road 2, certain redevelopment projects), some as token money; deals "already under negotiation or in the advanced stage."

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Presales growth: 25–30% for FY27** — reaffirmed twice despite Q1 at +20%: "we are confident overall in the full year, we will match our… guidance of 25% to 30% growth in our presales. Considering the full year of '27, we'll be at least 25% to 30% higher than the last year."
- **Collections: "similar growth, I would say, 25% to 30%"** for the year.
- **Launches this financial year: ~₹7,000–7,100cr of GDV (excluding Dubai)** — ODC additional tower; Andheri redevelopment (near Western Express Highway); **Sunteck Park Mira Road 2**; **one more tower at Vasai**; **1–2 towers at Naigaon**; **Sunteck Sky Park 2** and **Tower 2 at Sunteck City** specifically in the coming quarter.
- **Business development spend: to exceed FY26's >₹800cr** — "we are looking to, in fact, surpass this number… definitely this year also much more than the last year." ₹170cr already spent in Q1. Expect "some good acquisition BD announcements for sure."
- **Deliveries in FY27:** **Sunteck OneWorld**, plus new floors at **4th Avenue**, **1st Avenue** and **Pinnacle** — all to be constructed and delivered within the year, completing in **3–6 months** and monetised in the current year. Described as "substantial, very large delivery."
- **5th Avenue ODC:** residential construction started, **delivery ~3 years from now**; **commercial to start very soon and complete in 24–30 months** (presentation shows commercial revenue rising to ₹450cr by FY29).
- **Dubai (₹9,000cr GDV):** all regulatory approvals in place, project **launch-ready**; **timing recalibrated due to the ongoing situation** — no FY27/FY28 commitment given. Investment to date only **~₹200–225cr, no debt on the project**; surplus cash flow intended to be **repatriated to India for group growth**.
- **Fundraising:** the ₹2,000cr+ debt/equity board resolution is an **annual enabling resolution only** — "as on today, if you ask me, there is absolutely no planning of any fundraising."
- **Nepean Sea Road:** the big collections trigger once construction starts; RERA status not confirmed on the call.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Dubai as a low-cost, high-convexity option**: ~₹200–225cr of capital committed against ₹9,000cr of GDV, no debt, all approvals done, launch-ready — and the intent is to **repatriate the surplus to India for group growth**. The optionality costs almost nothing to hold.
- **Redevelopment** — Andheri (Western Express Highway) plus "certain redevelopment projects" funded within the Q1 ₹170cr BD spend.
- **Aggressive land banking / BD** — FY26 was the highest-ever BD year at >₹800cr, and FY27 is guided to surpass it, funded off a net-cash balance sheet.
- **Commercial rental annuity** at 5th Avenue ODC ramping to ₹450cr by FY29.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- **Reported EBITDA margin 35% (+9.5pp YoY)** and **PAT margin 22% (+4.2pp)** on nearly flat operating revenue — i.e. the margin expansion is mix and project-stage driven, not volume driven.
- **Embedded EBITDA margin of 35–40%** on both FY26 and Q1FY27 presales is the forward margin anchor; management ties reported profitability directly to revenue-recognition timing on those presales.
- The **balanced segment mix** (29/50/21) is presented as the reason the embedded margin holds — aspirational luxury growth has not diluted the blend.
- No input-cost or construction-cost commentary was offered on this call.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- **Net cash surplus ₹193cr generated after ₹170cr of BD spend** — the clearest statement of the operating model: BD is funded out of operating cash, not leverage.
- **Net debt/equity 0.07x**; AA rated; **no fundraising planned** — the ₹2,000cr+ board resolution is a routine annual enabler taken every year.
- Dubai surplus, when it comes, is earmarked for **repatriation into India for group growth**.
- BD is countercyclical by intent — FY26 was a record year and FY27 is guided higher.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and cash-focused, with a notable moment of integrity: when an analyst pointed out that the presentation's "to-be-launched GDV" definition (projects under approval) contradicted the statement that Dubai has all approvals, Kamal Khetan **immediately conceded** — "I appreciate your comment. You're totally right… I think we'll have to edit that" — rather than defending the slide. He also declined to date Dubai despite being pushed twice, which is the honest answer for a discretionary launch. The proactive move to split GDV into three buckets is a real disclosure improvement made unprompted. Against that, the call ran only 30 minutes with two questions per participant, and several follow-ups (new BD, Nepean Sea RERA) were cut off by the moderator on time.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
- **Balance sheet as the competitive weapon**: net debt/equity **0.07x**, **AA** rating from India Ratings (Fitch Group) — described as "among the strongest in Indian real estate" — while simultaneously generating a ₹193cr net cash surplus *after* ₹170cr of BD. This is what lets Sunteck buy land through a soft patch and hold Dubai off-market indefinitely.
- **Embedded margin already locked**: 35–40% EBITDA margin sits inside FY26 and Q1FY27 presales, so future reported profitability is substantially pre-determined by sales already made, not by future pricing.
- **ESG leadership as a genuine differentiator**: **GRESB 99/100** (benchmark 68) and **DJSI 78/100** (benchmark 30) — top-decile globally, and increasingly a screen for institutional capital and premium tenants.
- **Cash-flow-first operating discipline**, stated explicitly and consistently: "we run the business on cash flow, not accounting revenue."

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
1. **Dubai timing is entirely discretionary and open-ended.** ₹9,000cr of the ₹16,100cr "to-be-launched" GDV — over half — is a project management explicitly will not date. Any GDV-based valuation must haircut this.
2. **Q1 presales grew 20% against a 25–30% full-year guide** — the gap must be made up in the remaining three quarters, and it depends on the ₹7,100cr launch slate landing on schedule.
3. **Presentation error on the GDV definition**, self-acknowledged. Minor in substance, but it means the new three-way GDV disclosure needs re-reading once corrected.
4. **Collections lag presales structurally**, and the step-change depends on **Nepean Sea Road construction starting** — RERA status was asked about and not answered.
5. **Revenue-recognition optics**: operating revenue up only 2% YoY. Anyone reading the P&L rather than the cash flow will misjudge the quarter in both directions.
6. **Aspirational-luxury strength is rate-dependent** — management attributed it to lower interest rates; a rate reversal removes the driver.
7. **Rising BD spend against a soft launch cadence** — capital going into land while launches are pending is the classic real-estate timing risk, mitigated here by the net-cash position.
8. **Very short call (30 minutes)** with limited disclosure on construction costs, inventory, or project-level unsold stock.

That is a demand signal, not an inventory-release signal, and it makes the 25–30% full-year guide more credible once the ₹7,100cr slate actually launches.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Shareholding] As at 30 Jun 2026: promoter & promoter group 63.14%, foreign portfolio / institutional investors 18.12%, domestic institutions (MFs / insurance) 5.30%, public & others 13.42%; stated to be before conversion of warrants.
